newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan plans to restructure national airline.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan plans to restructure national airline.

text.p: Pakistan said on Monday it planned to restructure state-run Pakistan International Airlines Corporation (PIA) in fiscal 1997/98 (July-June).
The Privatisation Commission said in a newspaper notice that it was seeking financial advisers to supervise the process.
The government was considering "capitalisation or financial restructuring of its national flag carrier, Pakistan International Airlines, during the 1997/98 period," it said.

It said the government was planning a two-phase process to divest part of its share-holding in PIA. First it would sell a controlling block of shares to a strategic investor to operate the airline. Remaining shares would then be sold to the public.

PIA had a share capital of 3.88 billion rupees ($96.583 million) as of December 31. It showed an after-tax profit of 22.303 million rupees for the half-year ended December 31, compared to 182.54 million in the same period of 1995.

The Commission said the government aimed to promote efficient development of air transport and private sector participation in the industry, as well as to generate the required investment to upgrade and modernise PIA's fleet.
Financial advisers were needed to design, develop and implement the first phase of the process, it said.

"The financial adviser will be responsible for all activities related to the trade sale (or private placement) of shares through an equity increase in the airline to a strategic investor...and the strategy for the treatment of the subsidiaries."
The Commission said the existing equity base of PIA would be raised to 100 percent from 50 percent now.

It said it was seeking consortia led by first-class investment banks with experience in airline privatisation, restructuring, mergers and acquisitions. The consortia should include a leading law firm with expertise in documentation, and a specialised consulting firm in the air transport sector.
Applications expressing interest must be submitted by 1200 GMT (1700 local) on April 21.
